title: Tensorized KV cache/view reconstruction
hypothesis: Charged per-role Mirror coordinates around a shared compressed KV tensor can reconstruct aligned logical KV roles with a useful quality/serialized-byte frontier against PA35-style shared matrix-bank factors, after reconstruction cost is counted.
physical_object: per-role sequence-by-channel K and V cache tensors
mirror_coordinate: one float32 2D channel rotation angle per aligned role, stored in payload; angles are supplied task metadata, not learned
logical_multiplicity: six aligned role-specific K/V cache tensors from one shared factor pair, plus two unrelated roles represented privately

selection.method: uniform integer draw using Python secrets.randbelow over sorted P0 UNTESTED registry IDs, excluding completed worker IDs and paused families
selection.provenance_note: The pre-work draw record said 456 candidates and MA-330 at index 26. The saved ID-list reconstruction also has 456 IDs and MA-330 at index 26, but its file SHA-256 differs from the previously recorded fingerprint. Random draw provenance is retained; the fingerprint discrepancy is unresolved.

development.selection_metric: mean normalized attention output MSE; choose smallest rank with mean <= 1e-4, otherwise minimum mean MSE

quality.metric: normalized MSE of synthetic attention outputs against full teacher KV tensors

success_gate: All three fresh worlds have Mirror normalized attention-output MSE <= 1e-4, at least 10% fewer serialized bytes than PA35 control at matched quality, and decode MAC proxy <= 2x PA35.
failure_gate: Fresh quality fails, or Mirror has <10% byte advantage over best non-Mirror shared-factor control at matched quality, or decode MAC proxy >2x.
boundaries: Synthetic mechanism screen only; no natural language or pretrained model claims.
Angles are supplied task metadata; no learned-code claim.
The teacher intentionally contains six rotated aligned roles and two unrelated private roles.
No optimizer training; factors are direct deterministic SVD fits.
